claim_text: Most of these verses speak of the soul delivered or brought up from Sheol: a living person rescued from death. Corrected 2026-10-04 (#1950): of 15 soul-delivered verses, 12 are rescue from dying; Psa 49:15 (set against the death of all, 49:10) and Psa 16:10 (as Act 2:27, 31 read it) look beyond death; Psa 89:48 says no one can. group: A6 natural (psychikos): set against the spiritual
claim_text: The verse puts soul and spirit beside joints and marrow, which are adjacent, and its end point is the heart: "discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart". It shows closeness that only the word can divide. It is one of several places the words part; others are added (1Co 15:45; 1Co 14:14–15; the *psychikos* / *pneumatikos* contrast in 1Co 2:14; 15:44–46) (dep §3.4; B §8)
